## What this pull request does

Adds new record(s) for CVE(s) that are not yet in `CVE-json/`.

A pull request can only add records. To change an existing record, add a field or a new allowed
value, or submit a different version of a CVE that already exists, open an issue instead. The
maintainers decide, so that every record stays consistent.

## Checklist

- [ ] Every file is named `CVE-YYYY-N.pavd.json`, sits in `CVE-json/`, and is a NEW file
- [ ] `contributed_by` is `{"source": "community", "github": "<your account>", "pull_request": <this number>, "date": "<the day you open the pull request, YYYY-MM-DD>"}`
- [ ] `python scripts/validate_records.py CVE-json/<your files>` reports every record valid
- [ ] Only `CVE-json/` files are added; `index.json`, `stats.json` and `CHANGELOG.md` are regenerated by the maintainers
- [ ] The record follows the schema exactly: no extra fields, no `meta`
- [ ] `classification_reason` and every `rationale` explain this CVE only
- [ ] Attack-chain steps are conceptual: no commands, payloads or exploit code
- [ ] Sources are public (NVD, MITRE, vendor advisory)
